body.statement:
Let \(\ell=0\), let \(A\subseteq X\), and suppose \(\mathcal I_A^{\mathrm{atom}}\subseteq\mathcal I\).  For every response-kernel tuple \(\mathbf K\) generated by a square exact-support mechanism with arbitrary independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources, the observational law identifies the unordered projective row orbit \(\mathscr R(Q)\), the bipartite graph \(\mathbb G_b(\mathscr R(Q))\), and \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathscr R(Q))\).  For each \(i\in A\), the atomic kernel identifies \(T_i\) as the unique linear translation parameter satisfying \(K_{\{i\}}(x)=\tau_{T_ix}K_{\{i\}}(0)\); no expectation is required.  Lifting every residual-unmixing row \(v\) by \(\Lambda_i(v,T_i)=(v,-vT_i)\) recovers exactly the projective rows of \(Q\) except \([Q_{i,:}]\).  Hence \(\rho_i(\Pi_A\mathbf K)=[Q_{i,:}]\), normalization at coordinate \(i\) gives \(\operatorname{rec}_i(\Pi_A\mathbf K)=\operatorname{row}_i(B)\), and
\[
 \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ker}}(\Pi_A\mathbf K)
 =\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{row}}(\Pi_A\mathbf K)
 =\{\mu\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathscr R(Q)):
 \mu([Q_{i,:}])=i\text{ for every }i\in A\}.
\]
For \(A=\varnothing\) this is the observational perfect-matching representation; for \(A=X\), the full atomic family leaves only the true matching and recovers every row of \(B\).
body.proof_tex:
When \(\ell=0\), \(C=Q^{-1}\) is square and invertible.  The observational law is the square mixture \(X=C\varepsilon\) of mutually independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources.  By \(\text{lem:square-ica-uniqueness}\), its law determines the unordered projective columns of \(C\), equivalently
\[
 \mathscr R(Q)=\{[Q_{r,:}]:r\in X\}.
\]
Invertibility makes the row classes distinct.  Their zero patterns determine \(\mathbb G_b\), and its definition determines \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

Fix \(i\in A\) and put \(U=X\setminus\{i\}\).  The intervention-pushforward lemma gives
\[
 K_{\{i\}}(x)=\mathcal L(Q_{U,U}^{-1}\varepsilon_U+T_ix),
 \qquad T_i=-Q_{U,U}^{-1}Q_{U,i}.                                    \tag{15}
\]
Taking \(x=0\) fixes the residual law.  The translation-rigidity lemma proves that \(T_i\) is the unique linear map translating that law to all the other kernels in (15), even when the sources have no moments.

At zero, (15) is a square invertible mixture of the \(n-1\) unaffected independent non-Gaussian sources.  Square ICA uniqueness identifies the projective rows of its unmixing matrix \(Q_{U,U}\).  If \(v=Q_{r,U}\) for \(r\in U\), then
\[
 vT_i=Q_{r,U}(-Q_{U,U}^{-1}Q_{U,i})=-Q_{r,i}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \Lambda_i(v,T_i)_U=Q_{r,U},\qquad
 \Lambda_i(v,T_i)_i=-vT_i=Q_{r,i}.
\]
The lifted residual classes are exactly \(\{[Q_{r,:}]:r\ne i\}\), whose unique complement in the observational orbit is \([Q_{i,:}]\).  Looplessness gives \(Q_{ii}=1\), so normalization at coordinate \(i\) returns
\[
 e_i^{\mathsf T}-Q_{i,:}=\operatorname{row}_i(B).
\]

It remains to compare matchings.  Every observational matching normalizes a row-scaled permutation of \(Q\): for a permutation matrix \(P\) and nonsingular diagonal \(\Delta\),
\[
 Q^\mu=\Delta P Q,\qquad \varepsilon^\mu=\Delta P\varepsilon.       \tag{16}
\]
Scaling and permutation preserve independence, nonconstancy, and non-Gaussianity without any location or moment hypothesis, and (16) reproduces the observational law.  If \(\mu([Q_{i,:}])=i\), then \(P\) fixes row \(i\) and restricts to a permutation \(P_U\) of \(U\).  Hence
\[
 Q^\mu_{U,U}=\Delta_UP_UQ_{U,U},\quad
 Q^\mu_{U,i}=\Delta_UP_UQ_{U,i},\quad
 \varepsilon^\mu_U=\Delta_UP_U\varepsilon_U,
\]
which implies
\[
 -(Q^\mu_{U,U})^{-1}Q^\mu_{U,i}=-Q_{U,U}^{-1}Q_{U,i},\qquad
 (Q^\mu_{U,U})^{-1}\varepsilon^\mu_U=Q_{U,U}^{-1}\varepsilon_U.     \tag{17}
\]
Thus any observational matching satisfying all row constraints generates all required atomic kernels with the one global representation (16).  Conversely, a kernel-compatible matched mechanism must, by the recovery just proved from the common kernel tuple, assign the uniquely recovered class \([Q_{i,:}]\) to label \(i\) for every \(i\in A\).  This proves the displayed matching equality.  The conclusions for \(A=\varnothing\) and \(A=X\) follow immediately.
body.justification: Atomic kernels recover response slopes by translation uniqueness and thereby impose exactly one row-label constraint per intervention, even for source laws without expectations.
body.gap: Sharifian et al.'s published row-recovery clause does not itself state the full response-kernel lift or matching-set equality used here.
body.consumer: The general compiler has a concrete square-model audit, and a full atomic family recovers every structural row.
